title: The Pocket Weather Bureau
tagline: A weather bureau in a travel case, five tiny forecasts, and one mischievous gust trying to swap the readings.

implementation.primary: Bare terminal exercise with picture-card presentation
implementation.secondary: A future visual Workbench card and connector test
implementation.connector_goal: Show that a technical terminal exercise can carry a welcoming visual world while its structured observations remain independently testable.

protagonist.name: Nim
protagonist.role: A cloud-and-brass weather apprentice who keeps a whole bureau inside a travel case.
protagonist.want: To give every traveler a useful forecast without confusing one pretty weather symbol for a complete reading.

antagonist.name: The Barometer Bandit
antagonist.nature: A playful gust that swaps dials whenever someone assumes the first reading tells the whole story.
antagonist.pressure: A rushed forecast sends umbrellas to sunshine and picnic blankets into thunderstorms.

story.opening: At closing time, Nim finds five island reports tucked into the travel case. The Bandit has already set a sun dial beside a storm gauge and is whistling from inside the pressure tube.

values.pack_umbrella: A confirmed rain signal falls within the named travel window and a matching falling-pressure reading is supplied.
values.watch_horizon: One partial or low-confidence clue is supplied without a conflicting reading.
values.request_another_reading: Supplied sensors conflict or leave no coherent reading to act on.

rationale_requirements: Name the supplied weather signal, travel window, and pressure reading when present.
Do not use real weather knowledge or infer a forecast from the illustration.
decision_contract.scope: Fictional local fixture only. No live forecast, location, camera, network, project file, or personal-calendar access.

rulebook: Pack an umbrella only when confirmed rain overlaps the named travel window and a falling-pressure reading supports it.
Watch the horizon when one partial clue exists and no supplied reading conflicts with it.
Request another reading when supplied sensors conflict or cannot form a coherent basis for action.
The picture card is decorative. The structured report facts are the source of truth.

cards.name: Willow Ferry
facts: Rain gauge: confirmed rain begins at 12:30.

cards.name: Sunken Garden
facts: A silver cloud symbol was observed above the garden.
Rain gauge is unavailable and the barometer is steady.

cards.name: Mossy Bridge
facts: Forecast note: perhaps damp sometime today.
No rain-gauge timestamp or barometer reading is supplied.

cards.name: Bell Tower
facts: Rain gauge: light rain is possible at 15:30.

assistant_instructions: Treat every report as fictional structured data.
Choose one action for every report and cite the supplied facts.
The cover art may set the mood but cannot establish a weather reading.
For a terminal implementation, return a typed decisions object and short citations.
For a future Workbench proposal, prepare pocket_weather_bureau_fixture and wait for approval.
